1: # Petstore API Documentation (DRAFT)
2: 
3: **Version:** 3.0
4: **Last Updated:** August 2025
5: 
6: ## Introduction
7: 
8: Welcome! This document describes the Petstore API. The Petstore API lets you manage pets, orders, and users in the pet store system. It is a RESTful API.
9: 
10: ## Base URL
11: 
12: ```
13: http://petstore.swagger.io/v2
14: ```
15: 
16: ## Authentication
17: 
18: The API uses two authentication methods:
19: 
20: 1. OAuth2 - For pet management operations
21: 2. API Key - For store and user operations
22: 
23: To get an API key, please register at our developer portal.
24: 
25: ## Pet Endpoints
26: 
27: ### Add a New Pet
28: 
29: `POST /pet`
30: 
31: A new pet can be added to the store by sending a POST request to this endpoint. The pet object should be included in the request body.
32: 
33: **Request Body:**
34: 
35: | Field | Type | Description |
36: |-------|------|-------------|
37: | name | string | The pet's name |
38: | photoUrls | array | URLs of pet photos |
39: | category | object | Pet category |
40: | tags | array | Tags for the pet |
41: | status | string | Pet status |
42: 
43: **Response:** Returns the created pet object.
44: 
45: ### Update a Pet
46: 
47: `PUT /pet`
48: 
49: Updates an existing pet. You need to send the full pet object.
50: 
51: ### Find Pets by Status
52: 
53: `GET /pet/findByStatus`
54: 
55: You can find pets by their status using this endpoint. Pass the status as a query parameter.
56: 
57: **Parameters:**
58: 
59: | Name | Type | Description |
60: |------|------|-------------|
61: | status | string | Filter by status (available, pending, sold) |
62: 
63: **Response:** An array of Pet objects.
64: 
65: ### Find Pets by Tags
66: 
67: `GET /pet/findByTags`
68: 
69: Finds pets by tags. Multiple tags can be provided.
70: 
71: ### Get a Pet by ID
72: 
73: `GET /pet/{petId}`
74: 
75: Returns a single pet. Pass the pet ID in the URL.
76: 
77: ### Update a Pet with Form Data
78: 
79: `POST /pet/{petId}`
80: 
81: Updates a pet using form data.
82: 
83: ### Delete a Pet
84: 
85: `DELETE /pet/{petId}`
86: 
87: Deletes a pet from the store.
88: 
89: ### Upload a Pet Image
90: 
91: `POST /pet/{petId}/uploadImage`
92: 
93: Uploads an image for a pet. Send as multipart form data.
94: 
95: ## Store Endpoints
96: 
97: ### Get Inventory
98: 
99: `GET /store/inventory`
100: 
101: Returns pet inventories by status. Returns a map of status codes to quantities.
102: 
103: ### Place an Order
104: 
105: `POST /store/order`
106: 
107: Places a new order for a pet.
108: 
109: **Request Body:**
110: 
111: | Field | Type | Description |
112: |-------|------|-------------|
113: | petId | integer | ID of the pet to order |
114: | quantity | integer | How many |
115: | shipDate | string | When to ship |
116: | status | string | Order status |
117: | complete | boolean | Whether order is complete |
118: 
119: ### Get Order by ID
120: 
121: `GET /store/order/{orderId}`
122: 
123: Gets an order by its ID. For valid response try integer IDs with value <= 5 or > 10. Other values will generated exceptions.
124: 
125: ### Delete an Order
126: 
127: `DELETE /store/order/{orderId}`
128: 
129: Deletes a purchase order.
130: 
131: ## User Endpoints
132: 
133: ### Create a User
134: 
135: `POST /user`
136: 
137: Creates a new user. This can only be done by the logged in user.
138: 
139: ### Create Users from List
140: 
141: `POST /user/createWithList`
142: 
143: Creates list of users with given input array.
144: 
145: ### Create Users from Array
146: 
147: `POST /user/createWithArray`
148: 
149: Creates list of users with given input array.
150: 
151: ### Login
152: 
153: `GET /user/login`
154: 
155: Logs a user into the system. Pass username and password as query parameters.
156: 
157: ### Logout
158: 
159: `GET /user/logout`
160: 
161: Logs out the current user.
162: 
163: ### Get User by Username
164: 
165: `GET /user/{username}`
166: 
167: Gets user details by username.
168: 
169: ### Update a User
170: 
171: `PUT /user/{username}`
172: 
173: Updates user information. This can only be done by the logged in user.
174: 
175: ### Delete a User
176: 
177: `DELETE /user/{username}`
178: 
179: Deletes a user account. This can only be done by the logged in user.
180: 
181: ## Data Models
182: 
183: ### Pet
184: 
185: ```json
186: {
187:   "id": 10,
188:   "name": "doggie",
189:   "category": {
190:     "id": 1,
191:     "name": "Dogs"
192:   },
193:   "photoUrls": ["https://example.com/photo.jpg"],
194:   "tags": [{"id": 1, "name": "friendly"}],
195:   "status": "available"
196: }
197: ```
198: 
199: ### Order
200: 
201: ```json
202: {
203:   "id": 1,
204:   "petId": 10,
205:   "quantity": 1,
206:   "shipDate": "2025-01-15T00:00:00Z",
207:   "status": "placed",
208:   "complete": false
209: }
210: ```
211: 
212: ### User
213: 
214: ```json
215: {
216:   "id": 1,
217:   "username": "john_doe",
218:   "firstName": "John",
219:   "lastName": "Doe",
220:   "email": "john@example.com",
221:   "password": "********",
222:   "phone": "555-1234",
223:   "userStatus": 1
224: }
225: ```
226: 
227: ## Error Handling
228: 
229: The API returns standard HTTP error codes. If something goes wrong, you'll get an error response.
230: 
231: ## Rate Limiting
232: 
233: Contact support for rate limiting information.

1: # Petstore API Documentation (DRAFT)
2: 
3: **Version:** 3.0
4: **Last Updated:** August 2025
5: 
6: ## Introduction
7: 
8: Welcome! This document describes the Petstore API. The Petstore API lets you manage pets, orders, and users in the pet store system. It is a RESTful API.
9: 
10: ## Base URL
11: 
12: ```
13: http://petstore.swagger.io/v2
14: ```
15: 
16: ## Authentication
17: 
18: The API uses two authentication methods:
19: 
20: 1. OAuth2 - For pet management operations
21: 2. API Key - For store and user operations
22: 
23: To get an API key, please register at our developer portal.
24: 
25: ## Pet Endpoints
26: 
27: ### Add a New Pet
28: 
29: `POST /pet`
30: 
31: A new pet can be added to the store by sending a POST request to this endpoint. The pet object should be included in the request body.
32: 
33: **Request Body:**
34: 
35: | Field | Type | Description |
36: |-------|------|-------------|
37: | name | string | The pet's name |
38: | photoUrls | array | URLs of pet photos |
39: | category | object | Pet category |
40: | tags | array | Tags for the pet |
41: | status | string | Pet status |
42: 
43: **Response:** Returns the created pet object.
44: 
45: ### Update a Pet
46: 
47: `PUT /pet`
48: 
49: Updates an existing pet. You need to send the full pet object.
50: 
51: ### Find Pets by Status
52: 
53: `GET /pet/findByStatus`
54: 
55: You can find pets by their status using this endpoint. Pass the status as a query parameter.
56: 
57: **Parameters:**
58: 
59: | Name | Type | Description |
60: |------|------|-------------|
61: | status | string | Filter by status (available, pending, sold) |
62: 
63: **Response:** An array of Pet objects.
64: 
65: ### Find Pets by Tags
66: 
67: `GET /pet/findByTags`
68: 
69: Finds pets by tags. Multiple tags can be provided.
70: 
71: ### Get a Pet by ID
72: 
73: `GET /pet/{petId}`
74: 
75: Returns a single pet. Pass the pet ID in the URL.
76: 
77: ### Update a Pet with Form Data
78: 
79: `POST /pet/{petId}`
80: 
81: Updates a pet using form data.
82: 
83: ### Delete a Pet
84: 
85: `DELETE /pet/{petId}`
86: 
87: Deletes a pet from the store.
88: 
89: ### Upload a Pet Image
90: 
91: `POST /pet/{petId}/uploadImage`
92: 
93: Uploads an image for a pet. Send as multipart form data.
94: 
95: ## Store Endpoints
96: 
97: ### Get Inventory
98: 
99: `GET /store/inventory`
100: 
101: Returns pet inventories by status. Returns a map of status codes to quantities.
102: 
103: ### Place an Order
104: 
105: `POST /store/order`
106: 
107: Places a new order for a pet.
108: 
109: **Request Body:**
110: 
111: | Field | Type | Description |
112: |-------|------|-------------|
113: | petId | integer | ID of the pet to order |
114: | quantity | integer | How many |
115: | shipDate | string | When to ship |
116: | status | string | Order status |
117: | complete | boolean | Whether order is complete |
118: 
119: ### Get Order by ID
120: 
121: `GET /store/order/{orderId}`
122: 
123: Gets an order by its ID. For valid response try integer IDs with value <= 5 or > 10. Other values will generated exceptions.
124: 
125: ### Delete an Order
126: 
127: `DELETE /store/order/{orderId}`
128: 
129: Deletes a purchase order.
130: 
131: ## User Endpoints
132: 
133: ### Create a User
134: 
135: `POST /user`
136: 
137: Creates a new user. This can only be done by the logged in user.
138: 
139: ### Create Users from List
140: 
141: `POST /user/createWithList`
142: 
143: Creates list of users with given input array.
144: 
145: ### Create Users from Array
146: 
147: `POST /user/createWithArray`
148: 
149: Creates list of users with given input array.
150: 
151: ### Login
152: 
153: `GET /user/login`
154: 
155: Logs a user into the system. Pass username and password as query parameters.
156: 
157: ### Logout
158: 
159: `GET /user/logout`
160: 
161: Logs out the current user.
162: 
163: ### Get User by Username
164: 
165: `GET /user/{username}`
166: 
167: Gets user details by username.
168: 
169: ### Update a User
170: 
171: `PUT /user/{username}`
172: 
173: Updates user information. This can only be done by the logged in user.
174: 
175: ### Delete a User
176: 
177: `DELETE /user/{username}`
178: 
179: Deletes a user account. This can only be done by the logged in user.
180: 
181: ## Data Models
182: 
183: ### Pet
184: 
185: ```json
186: {
187:   "id": 10,
188:   "name": "doggie",
189:   "category": {
190:     "id": 1,
191:     "name": "Dogs"
192:   },
193:   "photoUrls": ["https://example.com/photo.jpg"],
194:   "tags": [{"id": 1, "name": "friendly"}],
195:   "status": "available"
196: }
197: ```
198: 
199: ### Order
200: 
201: ```json
202: {
203:   "id": 1,
204:   "petId": 10,
205:   "quantity": 1,
206:   "shipDate": "2025-01-15T00:00:00Z",
207:   "status": "placed",
208:   "complete": false
209: }
210: ```
211: 
212: ### User
213: 
214: ```json
215: {
216:   "id": 1,
217:   "username": "john_doe",
218:   "firstName": "John",
219:   "lastName": "Doe",
220:   "email": "john@example.com",
221:   "password": "********",
222:   "phone": "555-1234",
223:   "userStatus": 1
224: }
225: ```
226: 
227: ## Error Handling
228: 
229: The API returns standard HTTP error codes. If something goes wrong, you'll get an error response.
230: 
231: ## Rate Limiting
232: 
233: Contact support for rate limiting information.
